entries.note: The access requests described here concern Marcus; the normalization adds Davis. “Scandalous” is a judgment of worth.

entries.test: Contemporaneous access policies and documented arrangements for Marcus and Davis's experiments would establish whether their analysis depended on access supplied by others.
entries.note: The source explains how Marcus and Davis obtained access; the normalization generalizes this to outside analysis overall.

entries.test: Published evaluations of models available by June 2022 on the six identified problem categories would show whether the general failures persisted despite individual examples being corrected.
entries.note: The normalized proposition omits “so far as I can tell,” although the separate conditions field preserves it.

entries.test: Public evaluations of GPT-3 and its June 2022 successors on factual and commonsense reasoning tasks would establish whether they remained unreliable interpreters of everyday situations.
entries.note: The surrounding examples and listed reasoning categories give the reliability claim a concrete behavioral reading.

entries.test: Repeated comparative testing of GPT-2 and GPT-3 on the same prompts would establish whether GPT-3 had higher correct-answer rates.
entries.note: The GPT-2-to-GPT-3 improvement is asserted firmly. The separate InstructGPT comparison is explicitly left uncertain.
“I see no reason … to think” is weaker than the categorical normalization. The post supplies no shared criterion for possessing a cognitive model of the world.

entries.test: Controlled scaling studies varying training-data volume while accounting for architecture, parameter count, and training methods would establish whether larger datasets primarily explained the improvements.
entries.note: The adjacent sentence supports the normalization's contrast with genuine comprehension.
Ease of finding failures is testable, but the full causal claim depends on an unspecified criterion for genuine comprehension.
The post does not establish what would distinguish a qualitative change from a sufficiently large quantitative improvement.
No shared test is supplied for distinguishing “real” understanding from successful behavior attributed to parroting.

entries.test: Documentation that GPT-4 met the architecture and access conditions, together with a timestamped record of Marcus and Davis's first day of testing, would establish whether they found many reasoning failures.
entries.note: GPT-4's release alone does not establish that the unrestricted-access antecedent occurred.
The surrounding forecast assumes essentially the same architecture with more data; the normalized sentence omits that condition. “Genuine causal model” lacks an agreed criterion here.
Reliability can be measured, but settling the stated cause requires a shared criterion for the causal world models he says are missing.
“I would be very surprised if … not” expresses likelihood rather than an unconditional prediction; the longer-prompt suggestion is also explicitly tentative.

entries.test: Public evaluations of language models without symbolic components on varied physical and psychological reasoning tasks would establish whether systematic weaknesses persist or robust competence provides a counterexample.
entries.note: In context, weakness has a behavioral reading grounded in the reasoning failures described throughout the post.

entries.test: Published responses and comparative scoring across the complete Technology Review question set would establish the size of InstructGPT's improvement and whether previously correct answers regressed.
entries.note: “More modest than one might have expected” is relative to expectations; “improves only modestly” makes an absolute claim.
He asserts that the result may have been a fluke, not that it was one.
